common_name: Climbing Old Blush Rose (Vigorous Climbing Sport of Old Blush China)

planting.note: Plant container or bare-root roses in spring near a sturdy fence, trellis, or arbor in well-drained soil in full sun; this vigorous climbing sport of Old Blush needs a large support and room to spread.

directions: Plant in well-drained, average soil in full sun against a large, sturdy support such as a fence, pergola, or arbor. This vigorous climbing sport of Old Blush, one of the four founding China roses brought to Europe in the late 1700s, carries the same historically significant repeat-blooming trait and semi-double, silvery-pink flowers that deepen with age and heat, but on long, arching canes capable of scaling a substantial structure. It blooms in flushes nearly continuously through the growing season, tolerates heat exceptionally well, and shows good resistance to black spot. Train and tie canes horizontally where possible to encourage more flowering laterals, and prune only to control size and remove dead or crossing wood, since it needs a season or two to establish before reaching its full climbing potential.

common_name: Climbing Souvenir de la Malmaison Rose (Vigorous Climbing Bourbon Sport)

planting.note: Set out own-root plants in spring or fall near a sturdy support in a site with excellent air circulation; this vigorous climbing sport of Souvenir de la Malmaison carries the same huge, fragrant blooms on long climbing canes.

directions: Plant in full sun with excellent air circulation in well-drained, fertile soil against a sturdy fence, pergola, or wall. This vigorous climbing sport of the famous 1843 Bourbon rose Souvenir de la Malmaison carries the same enormous, flat, quartered blush-pink blooms and rich old-rose fragrance as the bush form, but on long canes capable of covering a substantial structure. Like its parent, its densely petaled blooms can 'ball' and fail to open in prolonged Gulf Coast humidity, so siting it where morning sun dries the foliage quickly and air moves freely improves bloom quality. It reblooms in flushes from spring through fall; prune lightly after each flush to remove spent flowers, and avoid heavy pruning of the main canes, which reduces flowering and delays the climbing habit from filling in.

common_name: Madame Antoine Mari Rose (Antique Pink-Blush Tea Rose)

planting.note: Set out own-root plants in spring or fall; Madame Antoine Mari, introduced in 1900, is a classic antique tea rose valued for soft pink-blush blooms and reliable performance in poor soil.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained soil. Madame Antoine Mari, introduced in France in 1900, bears large, loosely double blooms in soft pink shading to a paler blush at the petal edges, carrying the classic fruity tea fragrance the class is prized for. Like other old tea roses it flowers nearly continuously from spring to frost, tolerates poor, sandy soil far better than modern hybrid teas, and shows good resistance to blackspot in humid Gulf South conditions. Long grown in Southern gardens with little care, it needs only light pruning in late winter to remove dead or crossing wood and control size.
